newsitem.title: USA: U.S. regrets failure of UN motion on China rights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. regrets failure of UN motion on China rights.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday said it deeply regretted the failure at the U.N. Human Rights Commission of a Western resolution criticising China's human rights record.

"This action is inconsistent with the fundamental principle the commission is charged to defend: that how a nation treats its citizens is the legitimate concern of all mankind," said a White House statement issued in New York, where President Bill Clinton was on a day-long visit.

Earlier, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had also expressed regret about the decision. The United States had been a co-sponsor of the resolution, which was proposed by Denmark, at the meeting of the commission in Geneva.
"We congratulate the government of Denmark for sponsoring the resolution and the others who co-sponsored it," Albright said in a speech at the U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis, Maryland.

For the seventh year since 1990, Western European countries and the United States failed to achieve even a vote on the issue in the 53-member body despite heavy lobbying, handing China a diplomatic triumph.
The Chinese delegation won a vote for a so-called "no-action motion" on the issue by 27 against 17 with nine countries, including Russia, abstaining, effectively blocking scrutiny of its record.

The White House statement said America had chosen to engage China across a broad range of issues because it is in U.S. interests to develop a "positive and constructive" relationship with a country that is home to a fifth of the world's population and plays an increasingly important role in world affairs.

"At the same time, it should be clearly understood that we will continue to speak out on important issues where we disagree, and one of the most important of these issues is human rights," the White House said.

"By taking a stand against human rights abuses, in China and around the world, we keep faith with those who champion these principles. We also maintain our leadership on human rights issues and express the deepest values of the American people," it said.
